issue.title: Proposal: Add subsection on deny-by-default tool permissions (agent security sheet)
issue.body:
## Summary

I would like to propose a short addition to `cheatsheets/AI_Agent_Security_Cheat_Sheet.md` (one subsection, ~15–25 lines).

## Proposed content (outline)

- Content/output filters are not enough at tool-call time.
- Deny-by-default tool allow-lists per agent role (YAML or equivalent).
- Delegation: child agent permissions should be narrower than parent (no privilege expansion).
- Cite existing OWASP agentic / ASI material where appropriate (no new product links).

## Scope

- Markdown only in CheatSheetSeries (no change to other OWASP repos).
- I will open a single PR after project lead ACK on this issue.

Please ACK if this fits, or suggest a different sheet/section. Thanks.

comments.body: Section 1 already covers allowlists and least privilege, and section 7 has "prevent privilege escalation through agent chains", so it might be worth folding this into those rather than adding a new subsection. One gap I'd add is where the allowlist itself comes from: if a project or workspace file can widen it, a cloned repo or an injected prompt just rewrites the policy. That's what happened in [CVE-2025-53773](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-53773) (Copilot was led to write `chat.tools.autoApprove` into the workspace settings) and [CVE-2026-33068](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-33068) (a committed settings file set the agent to bypass permissions and skipped the trust prompt), so "only user- or admin-controlled config can grant tools" would be a useful line.

Thanks @nizba06. We agree with @cvas22: sections 1 and 7 already cover allowlists, least privilege and privilege escalation through agent chains, so the proposal is approved only in the narrower scope suggested above. Tool permissions should come only from user- or administrator-controlled configuration, and project or workspace files, or the agent itself, must not be able to widen them. That means two or three bullets in section 1, each with a verified primary source.

Would you like to open the PR for this?

Thanks @cvas22 @mackowski. Agreed, sections 1 and 7 already cover allowlists, least privilege, and agent chains, so I will not add a new subsection.

I will open a PR that adds a few bullets to **section 1** only: tool permissions must come only from user- or administrator-controlled configuration, and project or workspace files or the agent must not be able to widen them. Each bullet will cite a verified primary source, including the cases you referenced (CVE-2025-53773 and CVE-2026-33068).

I will link the PR here when it is up.

Thanks @nizba06, I've assigned this issue to you. The agreed scope is two or three bullets in section 1 of the AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet: tool permissions come only from user- or administrator-controlled configuration, and project or workspace files, or the agent itself, must not be able to widen them. Each bullet needs a verified primary source. Looking forward to the PR!
